exam: Kerala PSC Junior Co-operative Inspector / Assistant etc.
paper: Question Paper 13/2026 (English medium, Set A) - Co-operative Law, Banking and Computer section (Q45-100)

questions.q: Minimum number of persons required to form a cooperative society under Cooperative Credit Societies Act, 1904 was
questions.e: The Co-operative Credit Societies Act, 1904 required at least 10 persons to form a society.

questions.q: One of the major features of the Model Cooperative Societies Bill, 1991 was
o: No rule making power to the government
Accepting funds from the government by way of equity
Power to the Registrar for the compulsory amendment of the by-laws
questions.e: As per the official key, the Model Co-operative Societies Bill, 1991 took away the government's rule-making power to make societies more autonomous.

questions.q: The Andhra Pradesh Mutually Aided Cooperative Societies Act was based on
questions.e: Andhra Pradesh's Mutually Aided Co-operative Societies Act, 1995 was modelled on the Model Co-operative Societies Bill, 1991.

questions.q: The authority responsible for the administration of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 1984 vests with
questions.e: Multi-State co-operative societies are administered by the Central Registrar of Co-operative Societies.

questions.q: Which is the supreme authority of a cooperative society under Kerala Cooperative Societies Act, 1969?
questions.e: Under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 the General Body of members is the supreme authority.

questions.q: The National Development Council (NDC) Resolution in 1956, was linked with
questions.e: The 1956 NDC resolution on co-operative development was tied to the Second Five-Year Plan.

questions.q: Under which banking system banks operate through a network of branches?
questions.e: In branch banking one bank works through many branches.

questions.q:
Statement I : Unit banking system is popular in the USA.
Statement II : Branch banking promotes uniform banking practices.
Choose the correct answer :
questions.e: Unit banking is common in the USA, and branch banking spreads uniform practices; both statements are true.

questions.q: Which deposit is included under CASA?
questions.e: CASA means Current Account and Savings Account deposits.

questions.q: Credit creation by commercial banks is mainly based on
questions.e: Banks create credit from primary deposits and the derived deposits that loans generate.

questions.q:
Statement I : RBI acts as banker to the government.
Statement II : RBI provides Ways and Means Advances to State Governments.
Choose the correct answer :
questions.e: RBI is banker to the governments and gives Ways and Means Advances to states for short-term cash gaps.

questions.q: Open Market Operations (OMO) refer to
o: Purchase and sale of government securities
questions.e: Open market operations are RBI's purchase and sale of government securities.

questions.q: Which of the following is a qualitative method of credit control?
questions.e: Moral suasion is a qualitative (selective) credit control; bank rate, CRR and SLR are quantitative.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India was established in the year
questions.e: RBI started working on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934.

questions.q: Name the banks which were merged to form the Imperial Bank of India in 1921?
o: Allahabad Bank, United Bank of India, Syndicate Bank
Bank of India, Central Bank of India, Punjab National Bank
Bank of Bombay, Bank of Bengal, Bank of Madras
Bank of Baroda, Canara Bank, Indian Bank
questions.e: The three Presidency Banks of Bombay, Bengal and Madras merged into the Imperial Bank of India in 1921.

questions.q:
Which of the statements regarding Regional Rural Banks are correct?
I. RRBs are primarily formed to lend to priority sectors in rural and semi-urban areas.
II. RRBs were established under the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
III. The ownership structure of RRBs is shared between the Central Government, State Government and the concerned Sponsor Bank.
o: Only Statements I and III are correct
Only Statements II and III are correct
Only Statements I and II are correct
Statements I, II and III are correct
questions.e: RRBs serve rural priority sectors and are owned by the Centre, the state and a sponsor bank; they were set up under the RRB Act, 1976, not the BR Act.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are the function/s of the Lead Bank under the Lead Bank Scheme?
o: Prepares and monitors District Credit Plans to meet credit needs in Agriculture, Micro and Small Enterprises etc.
Organizes District Consultative Committees and Block Level Bankers' Committees to align banks and government agencies
Acts as a consortium leader for all banks in its assigned district, co-ordinating efforts for development
questions.e: Under the Lead Bank Scheme the lead bank prepares district credit plans, runs district/block committees and coordinates all banks in the district.

questions.q: The National Credit Council (NCC), constituted in India, primarily aimed to
o: Formulate monetary policy, regulate money supply and help in the control of inflation to protect currency value
Act as a statutory regulator of commercial banks under the RBI Act, 1934
Advise the government and RBI on the allocation of institutional credit in accordance with national priorities
Directly supervise credit appraisal and sanction by public sector banks
questions.e: The National Credit Council advised on allocating bank credit according to national priorities.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the recommendations of the Narasimham Committee (1991).
Statement I : The Committee recommended the introduction of prudential norms relating to income recognition, asset classification and capital adequacy for banks.
Statement II : The Committee advocated greater operational autonomy for public sector banks and a reduction in Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) and Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) to enhance banks' lending capacity.
Statement III : The Committee recommended the continuation of government-administered interest rate policy for banks, rather than allowing market forces of demand and supply to determine rates.
Which of the above statements are correct?
o: Only Statement I and Statement II are correct
Only Statement II and Statement III are correct
Only Statement I and Statement III are correct
questions.e: Narasimham Committee (1991) recommended prudential norms and lower SLR/CRR, but it wanted interest rates deregulated, not administered.

questions.q: Which of the following was not the objective behind permitting the entry of new generation private sector banks in India?
o: To promote competition, efficiency and technological upgradation in the banking system
To increase government ownership in banking and to reduce the role of RBI in banking regulation
To strengthen the banking system and make reach banking services to almost all areas of the country
To promote financial inclusion for bringing more people into the formal banking system
questions.e: New private banks were allowed to increase competition and efficiency, not to raise government ownership or weaken RBI.

questions.q: Which of the following is a direct initiative of the Reserve Bank of India to promote financial inclusion in India?
o: Launch of Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)
Implementation of Self-Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme (SHG-BLP)
Introduction of Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme
Introduction of Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account (BSBDA)
questions.e: The Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account was introduced by RBI itself to promote financial inclusion.

questions.q: Certain challenges are often faced by banks that come across with merger or acquisition. Identify a major challenge from the following.
o: Excess liquidity due to increase in the deposits
Difficulty in integrating different organizational cultures and systems
questions.e: Merging banks often struggle to combine different work cultures and IT systems.

questions.q: After recent amendments through the Banking Regulation (Amendment) Act, 2020 and the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2024/2025, which of the following is correct?
o: RBI's regulatory powers over cooperative banks have been reduced and the threshold of “substantial interest” has been brought down from Rs. 5 lakh to Rs. 1 lakh

RBI's powers over cooperative banks have been strengthened, and the definition of “substantial interest” threshold is proposed to be increased from Rs. 5 lakh to Rs. 2 crore to reflect current economic conditions
Cooperative banks are fully removed from the scope of the Banking Regulation Act
The concept of “substantial interest” has been deleted from the Act
questions.e: The amendments strengthened RBI's control over co-operative banks and proposed raising the 'substantial interest' limit from Rs. 5 lakh to Rs. 2 crore.

questions.q: For a company to commence or carry on banking business in India under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, it must
o: Obtain a licence from the Registrar of Companies
Obtain a licence from the Reserve Bank of India under Section 22
Take approval only from the Ministry of Finance
questions.e: Section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act requires a licence from RBI to carry on banking.

questions.q: Under Section 17 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, every banking company (other than certain exempted ones) must transfer to its Reserve fund each year
o: Not less than 2% of its net profits
Not less than 10% of its gross profits
Not less than 20% of its profits before declaration of dividend
A fixed amount prescribed by the Central Government
questions.e: Section 17 requires at least 20% of profit (before dividend) to be moved to the reserve fund.

questions.q: Acquisition of the undertaking of a banking company under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 can generally be done by the Central Government
o: Only on the recommendation of SEBI
After consultation with the Reserve Bank of India and following the prescribed procedure
Only if all shareholders consent unanimously
questions.e: The Centre can acquire a banking company's undertaking only after consulting RBI and following the Act.

questions.q: Which is not typically considered a special type of bank customer requiring specific documentation?
questions.e: Married women do not need special documents; minors, lunatics and unregistered firms do.

questions.q: In a joint bank account operated on "Either or Survivor" basis, upon death of one holder
o: Account is frozen until succession certificate
Survivor can operate and close the account
questions.e: In an 'Either or Survivor' account the surviving holder can operate and close it.

questions.q: For opening a bank account of a partnership firm, the bank typically requires
o: Partnership deed and resolution authorizing signatories
No documents if partners are known
questions.e: A firm's account needs the partnership deed and a mandate naming who can sign.

questions.q: Which is a key obligation of a banker towards the customer?
o: To disclose customer's account details to third parties without consent
To honour customer's cheques if sufficient funds are available and no legal stop is in place
To invest customer's money without permission
questions.e: A banker must honour cheques when funds are enough and there is no legal bar.

questions.q: Which of the following can endorse a bill of exchange?
questions.e: As per the official key, the payee (as holder) endorses the bill to transfer it.

questions.q: Who directs the bank to credit the cheque amount only into the bank account of the payee named on the cheque and not pay it in cash or to anyone else?
questions.e: An 'Account Payee' crossing tells the bank to credit only the named payee's account.

questions.q: Who can convert a general crossing of cheque into a special crossing of cheque?
questions.e: Under Section 125 of the NI Act, the holder can convert a general crossing into a special one.

questions.q: In which type of mortgage, the sale becomes void if the loan is repaid?
questions.e: In a mortgage by conditional sale, the sale becomes void when the loan is repaid.

questions.q:
Who introduced KCC?
i. Central Government
ii. State Government
iii. Local Self Government
iv. All of the above
questions.e: The Kisan Credit Card scheme was introduced by the Central Government (with RBI and NABARD) in 1998.

questions.q: Which is the apex institution for rural credit and financing?
questions.e: NABARD is the apex institution for agriculture and rural credit.

questions.q: Which among the following is not a feature of micro financing?
questions.e: Microfinance serves low-income people, so targeting high-income groups is not its feature.

questions.q: Who first launched Self Help group bank linkage programme in India?
questions.e: NABARD launched the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme in 1992.

questions.q: Which payment system in India allows 24 × 7 instant fund transfer including holidays?
questions.e: IMPS gives instant transfers 24x7, including holidays.

questions.q: Which card payment system is India's domestic card network promoted by NPCI?
questions.e: RuPay is India's own card network run by NPCI.

questions.q: In which system are interbank funds settled individually and in real time?
questions.e: RTGS settles each transaction individually and in real time.

questions.q: Which system enables electronic image-based cheque clearing instead of physical movement of cheques?
questions.e: Cheque Truncation System (CTS) clears cheques using images instead of moving paper.

questions.q: CAMELS rating of banks is used to assess
questions.e: CAMELS (Capital, Assets, Management, Earnings, Liquidity, Sensitivity) rates a bank's financial health.

questions.q: Which of the following forms part of Tier I Capital?
questions.e: Paid-up equity capital is core Tier I capital; the others are Tier II.

questions.q: An asset becomes a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) when interest or principal remains overdue for more than
questions.e: A loan becomes an NPA when interest or principal is overdue for more than 90 days.

questions.q: Which Act empowers banks to recover dues by enforcing security interest without court intervention?
questions.e: The SARFAESI Act, 2002 lets banks enforce security without going to court.

questions.q: Consider page reference string 1, 2, 0, 2, 5, 6, 2 with 3-page frames. Find the number of page faults using FIFO Page Replacement Algorithm.
questions.e: FIFO: 1, 2, 0 fault; 2 hits; 5, 6 and 2 each fault, giving 6 page faults.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of using overlays in memory management?
o: To increase the physical memory size
To allow programs larger than memory to execute
questions.e: Overlays let a program larger than memory run by loading only needed parts.

questions.q: A device that can interconnect two different networks having different protocols
questions.e: A gateway connects networks that use different protocols.

questions.q: What happens during a Denial of Service (DoS) attack?
o: Data is permanently deleted from the system
A system or network is made unavailable by overwhelming it with traffic
questions.e: A DoS attack floods a system with traffic so real users cannot use it.

questions.q: Section 67A of the Information Technology Act deals with
o: Publishing or transmitting material containing sexually explicit acts in electronic form
questions.e: Section 67A of the IT Act punishes publishing sexually explicit material electronically.

questions.q: Web crawlers in search engines are programs that
o: Automatically browse the internet to collect and update web page information
Search information only when users type a query
questions.e: Web crawlers automatically browse the web to collect and update page data for the search index.

questions.q: Which control structure allows you to choose between multiple alternatives?
questions.e: Switch-case selects one of many alternatives.

questions.q: Which type of storage device mainly benefits from disk defragmentation?
questions.e: Defragmentation helps hard disk drives, where scattered files slow down the moving read head.

questions.q: Arrange the following memory types in decreasing order of speed
questions.e: Speed order is registers > cache > RAM > hard disk.

questions.q:
Study the table given below and answer the question :
Software — Example
A — Windows
B — MS Word
C — WinZip
D — MySQL
Which of the following correctly classifies the software listed in the table?
o: A and B – System software; C and D – Application software
A and C – System software; B and D – Application software
A and D – System software; B and C – Application software
questions.e: Windows and WinZip (utility) are system software; MS Word and the fourth item are application software.
